edges.reason: T02's dispatch reads the webhook_url field that T01 adds to the todo record; T02 also touches app/api.py (mark_done) where T01 works (create_todo), so the ordering resolves the shared-file overlap as well
T03's E2E gates exercise the registration write path end to end and can only run after T01's store/API change exists
T03's E2E gates exercise the dispatch boundary (including the raising-dispatcher failure scenario) and can only run after T02's mark_done change exists

unlock_contracts.rationale: frozen in stage 1 and carried forward: both leaves build against the exact GET /todos key set without waiting on each other
frozen (additive) at stage-2 contract time: T02 can code against the webhook_url field spec before T01's store change lands
frozen dispatch contract: T02's implementation is fully specified up front

contract_bindings.rationale: the api layer (app/api.py) implements C1; T01 is the first owner of that file and its forbidden_scope explicitly protects list_todos' frozen response shape; T02/T03 consume the unchanged shape
T01 implements the store-side additive change (webhook_url) in app/store.py
T02 implements the done-notification dispatch in mark_done over the existing dispatcher

seam_bindings.rationale: handler->store boundary: T01 crosses it on the registration write path (create_todo -> store.add), T02 on the done read/mutate path (store.get -> transition)

mark_done->dispatch boundary: its input side (webhook_url on the done record) is T01's deliverable across the shared api/store surface, and its call side (api handler -> WebhookDispatcher) is implemented by T02; the stage-4 e2e task re-verifies the seam including its failure scenario

collisions_handled: T01 and T02 both own app/api.py (create_todo vs mark_done) — ordered T01 -> T02, which resolves the ownership overlap; no other path overlaps exist between the two leaves
free_parallelism_trades: no parallelism is possible with two ordered leaves; the single edge is a real data dependency (webhook_url field), not fear-based serialization — the task list is not artificially split to create groups
